messages:
Maria Lopez: Quickstart PR WIP — trimming auth examples and simplifying the hello-world flow. I removed the long legacy API_KEY section and tried to standardize on SDK v5 patterns. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4823
Kevin Tran: Looking now. Do we need to keep the curl example at all? It looks like it duplicates the SDK snippet and is outdated. :thinking_face:
Jen O'Neill: We should keep one tiny curl for users who just want a quick smoke test, but make it minimal and point to the SDK for real usage. Suggest: a 2-line curl that shows bearer token and body only.
Samir Patel: Agree. Also the Docker deploy in the quickstart still uses env var API_KEY in docker-compose. We should switch to passing a token file or reference to secret manager for the secure path, but doc-level quickstart can use ".env" with clear note.
Maria Lopez: Good call. Proposed changes in the PR:
```
# old (remove)
export API_KEY=sk-OLD
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Replace with:
```
# minimal curl smoke test
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Hello from quickstart"}'
```
Also SDK v5 example: use async await and example that works in both Node and bundlers.
Kevin Tran: The new SDK snippet looks good but please remove the raw JSON.stringify in the example body, make the request builder show typed params. Small nit: rename `resp` -> `result` for clarity.
Maria Lopez: Done in the next commit. I also added a short migration note for people coming from SDK v3/v4: a short table of changed function names and token usage.
Jen O'Neill: Can we add a one-line callout about streaming not being available on the free tier? Saw a support case today where folks tried it in quickstart and were confused.
Samir Patel: +1. Put it as a note under the streaming example: "Streaming requires a paid plan or dedicated deployment; fallback will return full response."
docs-bot: CI checks: docs build passed, linkcheck found 2 broken links (auth/legacy-token.md and examples/old-hello.md).
Maria Lopez: Thanks bot — fixed both links and updated the redirect. One more thing: examples/hello-docker now mounts .env in Compose. I added a short security tip and removed the composed multi-service example to keep quickstart focused.
Kevin Tran: Reviewer request: @Jen, @Samir can you do a quick pass for accuracy and tone? I can approve after wording tweaks.
Jen O'Neill: Will review in ~1hr. Focus points: tone (keep it beginner friendly), and the sidebar callouts (security and streaming).
Samir Patel: I'll check the docker and secret manager snippet for the private deployment note.
Maria Lopez: Thanks team. If reviews look good I'll merge after CI green and then open a small follow-up to add a short migration script for internal engineering examples.
Kevin Tran: One more tiny ask — update the changelog line for this doc PR with the migration header so it's easy to find in release notes.
Maria Lopez: Added changelog entry. Will merge once Jen + Samir approve and CI is green. :thumbsup:
Jen O'Neill: Approved from me — wording adjusted for clarity.
Samir Patel: Approved — changed the Docker secret example to use a mounted token file and added a link to KMS docs.
Maria Lopez: Merged. Release note: docs v1.18.2 quickstart refresh — smaller auth examples, clearer SDK v5 snippets, docker security tip, streaming callout.
Maria Lopez: Follow-up ticket created for adding an interactive CodeSandbox example so people can try the SDK flow in-browser without installing. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/2114
Kevin Tran: Nice. Good cleanup all around. :tada:
